author: fester
body: Reachability probe for the transpiler plugs' builtin lookup. Like `cce-bands`, this chapter deliberately CITES NOTHING: a chapter that cites a foreword chapter resolves that chapter's definition and is transpiled as ordinary user code, which tests nothing about an emitter's builtin table.

author: fester
body: Several plugs looked a builtin up with a BINARY search over a hand-written list. A binary search requires the list to be ordered by the comparison it searches with, and those two disagreed: the lists are written alphabetically while `text-compare` orders by CCE code point, and CCE numbers letters by frequency. Names past the first inversion were unreachable, and an unreachable builtin does not fail loudly -- it falls through to the ordinary apply path and emits a call to a function the target language has never heard of.

author: fester
body: So this file's value is one line per builtin in the emitted text. A name the plug recognises appears in that language's spelling; a name it missed appears as a bare call to the Codex name. Diffing the emitted output across a change to the lookup is what turns "how many builtins are reachable" into a measurement rather than a simulation.

author: fester
body: The names are spread deliberately across the alphabet, because the defect makes a CONTIGUOUS tail unreachable rather than a scattered few. File and process builtins (`open-file`, `read-text`, `write-file`, `file-exists`, `process-exit`, `fork`, `await`) are NOT covered here: they carry effects this chapter does not take, and the lookup they go through is the same one.
